# T007 — Repair frontend Vite build-tool advisories

## Summary

Patched the compatible Vite 6 / Rollup 4 build chain and its vulnerable CSS/source-map transitive packages without changing application code, plugins, TypeScript or test behavior. The root audit fell from **3 critical / 31 high / 7 moderate / 3 low (44 affected package entries)** to **3 critical / 26 high / 7 moderate / 3 low (39 entries)**. The independent backend lock is unchanged: **0 critical / 6 high / 0 moderate / 0 low**. These are affected-package counts, not unique advisories.

## Changes

- `frontend/package.json`: raise the direct Vite floor from `^6.3.5` to `^6.4.3`, the first 6.x version beyond all four reported vulnerable ranges. Keep the existing SWC and React plugin releases: their Vite peer ranges include 6.x.
- `package.json`: align the explicitly pinned root Linux native Rollup optional dependency with the resolved patched Rollup version, 4.64.12, so a clean Linux install supplies the correct binary.
- `package-lock.json`: generated exclusively with npm install/update. Vite 6.4.1 → 6.4.3, Rollup and its Linux native binary 4.52.5 → 4.64.12, PostCSS 8.5.6 → 8.5.31, nanoid 3.3.11 → 3.3.20, source-map-js 1.2.1 → 1.2.2. npm also regenerated optional-platform Rollup records, updated `@types/estree` 1.0.8 → 1.0.9, and hoisted away redundant backend workspace lock entries in the *root* lock. No backend manifest or independent backend lock changes.

## Decisions

Fresh npm lock audits and `npm explain` on **2026-10-20** identify the parent chain `frontend → vite → rollup, postcss → nanoid/source-map-js`; Tailwind also uses PostCSS and source-map-js. `frontend → vitest → tinypool, @vitest/mocker` is a separate test-runner major migration. `@github/spark`, `@tailwindcss/vite`, both React plugins and Vitest 3 accept Vite 6; no plugin update or framework jump is needed. Used npm 11.19.0 on Node 24.21.0 (`PATH=/opt/node/24/bin:$PATH`). The [Node release schedule](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/Release/main/schedule.json) lists Node 24 LTS ending 2028-04-30. Sources for advisory ranges: the live npm audit response and the linked GitHub advisories below; minimum patches are the first versions beyond the audit ranges in each compatible line. Build-time path injection would require an attacker-controlled filename/plugin, dev-server file reads generally require exposure of the dev server, and CSS/source-map issues require untrusted CSS/maps; no such remote exposure was established by offline tests.

## Validation

All commands below ran after the last package/lock edit from the repository root with `PATH=/opt/node/24/bin:$PATH`. `.modernization-scratch/scan/` is ignored locally and holds `npm-..json`, `npm-backend.json` and `scanner.log`. The scan's exit **2** means two complete vulnerable targets, **not** exit **1** (incomplete).

| `npm test` | Pass **35/35**, backend 10 and frontend 25, 0 failed, 0 skipped. |
| `npm run lint --if-present` | Pass, 0 errors, 5 pre-existing warnings. |

| `bash /shared/skills/dependency-vulnerability-remediation/scripts/scan-dependencies.sh --output-dir .modernization-scratch/scan .` | Exit **2**; root **3 critical / 26 high / 7 moderate / 3 low**; backend **0 / 6 / 0 / 0**. No Vite, Rollup, PostCSS, nanoid or source-map-js findings in either lock. |

## Follow-ups and risks

- **Open, owner decision required; no suppression/acceptance:** root critical `shell-quote` ([GHSA-w7jw-789q-3m8p](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w7jw-789q-3m8p), [GHSA-395f-4hp3-45gv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-395f-4hp3-45gv)) belongs to frontend delivery tools (T008); `tinypool` and the derived `vitest` critical entry need a separate characterized Vitest major upgrade. `@vitest/mocker` moderate remains from the same test runner. Neither critical chain is claimed mitigated.
- Other root high affected entries: `@azure/static-web-apps-cli`, `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin`, `@typescript-eslint/parser`, `@typescript-eslint/type-utils`, `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree`, `@typescript-eslint/utils`, `adm-zip`, `axios`, `brace-expansion`, `braces`, `browserslist`, `chokidar`, `fast-glob`, `flatted`, `form-data`, `glob`, `joi`, `js-yaml`, `lodash`, `micromatch`, `minimatch`, `node-forge`, `nodemon`, `picomatch`, `tmp`, `typescript-eslint`; moderate `@humanfs/node`, `ajv`, `baseline-browser-mapping`, `fast-copy`, `follow-redirects`, `yaml` (plus mocker); low `@babel/core`, `cookie`, `devcert`. The backend's unchanged six high entries are `brace-expansion`, `braces`, `chokidar`, `minimatch`, `nodemon`, `picomatch`. All per-package advisory IDs, ranges, severities, parent effects and fix availability are in the dated raw scan JSON; derived entries do not represent independent advisories. Do not install audit's suggested obsolete nodemon downgrade. Follow up in the separately scoped delivery/dev/lint-tool tasks and final report.
- No live Azure or deployed dev-server reachability was verified. Build still emits the same three CSS optimizer warnings. npm printed warnings about deferred optional install scripts (`@swc/core`, `esbuild`, `keytar`), but clean install/build/tests pass; no script policy was changed.
